title: Weak survival of the contact process on nonamenable Cayley graphs
aliases: Separation of global and local contact-process critical values
decision_reason: Explicit Cayley formulation and independent specialist corroboration; exact-scope resolution comparisons and separated A26 self-pass completed. Await later batch refresh.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Ordinary one-type continuous-time contact process on an undirected Cayley graph.
problem_fingerprint.dimension: No Euclidean dimension; arbitrary infinite finitely generated group.
problem_fingerprint.domain: Every finite symmetric generating set excluding the identity, with positive edge Cheeger constant.
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: Homogeneous isotropic nearest-neighbor infection, no disorder, avoidance or additional species.
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: Initially only group identity infected; infinite graph, no boundary.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every specified nonamenable Cayley graph, the global critical infection rate is strictly below the local one.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Recovery 1; infection lambda per infected neighbor, not lambda divided by degree.
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: Positive probability of never-empty infection versus positive probability of infections at the origin at arbitrarily large times.
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Infinite graph fixed first; time tends to infinity. No finite-network limit.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Unconditional mathematical existence of a weak-survival interval; no algorithmic or critical-endpoint assertion.

statement_source_and_scope_match: LA06 slide 31 explicitly poses the finitely generated nonamenable group problem after defining isotropic rates; LY00 p. 34 poses the broader transitive version. SWNOTE equation (3) and p. 3 corroborate the Cayley model with fixed infection and variable death. Time rescaling reverses the threshold inequality without changing strictness.
proposed_statement_text: For every nonamenable Cayley graph from a finite symmetric generating set, must the ordinary contact process have strictly separated global and local survival thresholds?
applied_significance: Idealized SIS network epidemics and population persistence can persist globally without returning to monitored sites. The significance is foundational infinite-network behavior, not a finite-data forecast.
